recognize_zh: 骨髓切片中一個血管腔內有捲曲、帶狀、呈顆粒狀嗜鹼性（淡紫藍色）且無細胞的異物，周圍有少量纖維化基質與多核巨細胞，符合導管來源的親水性聚合物栓子（hydrophilic polymer embolus）。
features: Serpiginous, ribbon-like, folded acellular deposit of lightly granular basophilic material within a vascular space
Material is homogeneous-granular, nonrefractile, with small clear vacuoles at its edges
Few multinucleated foreign-body-type giant cells at the lower edge of the deposit
Surrounding loose fibrous/edematous stroma with scattered mononuclear cells
Background fatty marrow with bony trabecula; no necrosis or infarct in this field
describe_en: Bone marrow core biopsy shows a predominantly fatty marrow space adjacent to a bony trabecula. Within a vascular space there is a coiled, serpiginous, ribbon-like deposit of acellular, finely granular, pale basophilic material, surrounded by loose fibrous stroma and a few multinucleated foreign-body giant cells. There is no associated necrosis, infarct, or neoplastic infiltrate in this field. In a patient with prior endovascular catheterization, findings are consistent with a hydrophilic polymer (catheter coating) embolus.

ddx.vs: Calcium is dark purple, glassy-to-fractured and often refractile, whereas polymer emboli are pale, granular, basophilic laminated ribbons within vessels.
Fungi show discrete septate or pauciseptate hyphal walls highlighted by GMS/PAS, whereas this material is amorphous and laminated without true hyphal structures.
Cholesterol emboli leave biconvex needle-shaped clefts in arterioles rather than solid basophilic serpiginous material.
Gelatinous transformation is a pale, extravascular, finely fibrillary interstitial substance around atrophic fat, not a coiled intravascular deposit with giant cells.
